pr_body:
This adds support for returning POLLHUP and POLLERR flags. Also, for
listening sockets, also returns POLLIN when a client is connected.

Fixes #3449
pr_comments:
Sorry for taking so long to get back to this, and thanks for the detailed test script and comments.  I ran your test (polltry.py) on the latest version with the patch 318f874cda22567a55bb004434ed0ec891fd7d61 and that has fixed a few cases.  The remaining case that is fixed by this PR here is how to handle a socket in STATE_NEW, namely to set POLLHUP.  In 1e2a6a84a263e069d7be5f27d73e7fc124413fa5 I incorporated this behaviour into the existing logic, which can be seen to be a straightforward change that shouldn't impact any existing behaviour because it just sets an additional flag (POLLHUP) for a case that was not considered before (STATE_NEW).

The polltry.py test running on esp8266 still doesn't behave exactly the same as CPython on Linux, but it's closer.  One of the things to improve is that poll should set POLLHUP/POLLERR regardless of the requested flags.  But changing this behaviour will change how select.select works so needs to be done separately.

issue_context.title: Polling non-blocking socket for POLLOUT after receiving RST results in null pointer dereference
issue_context.body:
Please run the attached script in a esp8266 board with modifying the target address/port to a reachable host and closed port.

[poll.py](https://github.com/micropython/micropython/files/1490567/trys.py.txt)
comments:
Just fo rconvenience: this is the script:
```
import usocket
import uselect
import time

poller = uselect.poll()

s = usocket.socket()

s.setblocking(False)

ai = usocket.getaddrinfo('10.0.0.10', 5001)[0][-1]
try:
    s.connect(ai)
except Exception as e:
    print('{!r}'.format(e))

time.sleep_ms(100)

poller.register(s, uselect.POLLOUT)
print (poller.poll(1000))
poller.unregister(s)

s.close()

poller.register(s, uselect.POLLIN)
print (poller.poll(1000))
```

review_comments: Shouldn't this be `(socket->pcb.tcp != NULL && ...`?  Is it still writable if the pcb is NULL?

On posix systems, when a socket is closed, it is being writable, where a write operation will return an error.

https://gist.github.com/rkojedzinszky/cbb6710c0cd6b205eda6f32b4bfcd7fc
Why is this part removed, how is this "peer closed" state handled now?

The closed socket is handled with HUP/ERR flag.

Again check this: https://gist.github.com/rkojedzinszky/cbb6710c0cd6b205eda6f32b4bfcd7fc

Arguable, a listening socket is still "new" and not yet connecting because there's not necessarily anyone trying to connect to it.  What problem does this line solve?  Is there a test case that can be written which shows why this line should be here?

A listening socket will never be in other state other than new, but it should not return HUP or ERR anyway. Another condition will set HUP if the connection is not CONNECTING nor CONNECTED either.

Please find my simple test script here: https://gist.github.com/rkojedzinszky/cbb6710c0cd6b205eda6f32b4bfcd7fc
